item.research_question: How can oxygen defects in ceria nanocrystals be engineered for enhanced catalysis via a high-entropy oxide strategy?
item.material_system: Ceria-based nanocrystals with surface-confined atomic high-entropy oxide layers
item.processing_route: Colloidal synthesis at 220 °C, followed by annealing in air at 500 °C
item.test_conditions: CO oxidation, temperature-programmed reduction, and oxygen isotope exchange
key_findings: Introduction of transition-metal components to ceria enhances surface redox properties
Surface-confined atomic high-entropy oxide layers promote formation of surface oxygen vacancies
CuCoFeNiMn-CeO2 sample exhibits optimal CO oxidation capabilities
Enhanced configurational entropy facilitates activation of surface lattice oxygen
Surface oxygen vacancies are positively correlated with transition-metal substitution
item.mechanism: The strong covalency of the transition-metal–oxygen bonds at the high-entropy oxide–ceria interface promotes the formation of surface oxygen vacancies, enabling efficient oxygen activation and replenishment for enhanced CO oxidation capabilities
item.future_work: More work is anticipated to unravel the metal–oxygen covalency in mixed and entropy-stabilized metal oxides
quotes: The strong covalency of the transition-metal–oxygen bonds facilitates the formation of surface-confined oxygen vacancies
The enhanced configurational entropy affords a distinct route to activating surface lattice oxygen
